// C:\workspace\SONIFY PLUGIN natura\src\GrexWidgets.h
#pragma once
//==============================================================================
//  GrexWidgets.h  -  the Grex synthesis-department controls, brought over as
//  they are: GoldSlider (the locked-geometry vertical slider), the velocity
//  curve display and the frame / button styling.  Only the palette moved
//  (Theme::Gold) and GoldSlider gained host gesture brackets.
//==============================================================================
#include <JuceHeader.h>
#include "Theme.h"

namespace VelCurve
{
    static constexpr float kMaxGamma = 2.5f;

    inline float gammaFor (float curve) noexcept
    {
        return std::pow (kMaxGamma, -juce::jlimit (-1.0f, 1.0f, curve));
    }

    /** 0..1 in, 0..1 out.  The shape, without MIDI's integer edges - the
        display draws this and apply() rounds it. */
    inline float shape (float x, float curve) noexcept
    {
        if (std::abs (curve) < 1.0e-3f) return x;
        return std::pow (juce::jlimit (0.0f, 1.0f, x), gammaFor (curve));
    }

    /** A MIDI velocity through the curve.  Never returns 0 for a note that was
        struck: velocity 0 is a note-OFF and turning a quiet hit into one would
        strand it. */
    inline int apply (int velocity, float curve) noexcept
    {
        if (velocity <= 0 || std::abs (curve) < 1.0e-3f) return velocity;
        const float out = shape ((float) velocity / 127.0f, curve) * 127.0f;
        return juce::jlimit (1, 127, (int) std::lround (out));
    }
}


/** The curve, drawn and draggable.  Vertical drag bends it; double-click
    returns to linear.  Small enough to live in half a column. */
class VelCurveDisplay : public juce::Component
{
public:
    std::function<void(float)> onChange;

    //==========================================================================
    /** The ENERGY offset currently in force on this slot's bank, 0 for none.

        THE READOUT SHOWS THE SUM, THE SLOT STORES ITS OWN VALUE.  Those are two
        different things on purpose, and conflating them was the design that got
        rejected: writing the offset back into the slot makes a performance
        control destructive.  velCurve is clamped, so a slot near an edge loses
        ground on every sweep - down 40 from 30 clamps at 0, back up 40 lands at
        40, and ten points of voicing are gone with nothing to say so.  One verse
        is enough to start it.

        So the offset stays separate and the ENGINE adds it, which it already
        does: two velocity curves in sequence add their curve values exactly.
        This only teaches the display to agree with the engine, so what you read
        is what is sounding, and moving ENERGY back leaves the slot untouched.

        Dragging still edits the BASE.  The drag applies to the number on screen
        and the base is back-computed, so what you set is what you see - which is
        the whole reason the sum is displayed rather than the base. */
    void setEnergyOffset (float c)
    {
        if (std::abs (c - energyOffset) < 1.0e-4f) return;
        energyOffset = c;
        repaint();
    }

    /** What the engine will actually apply: the slot's own curve plus ENERGY. */
    float effectiveCurve() const noexcept
    { return juce::jlimit (-1.0f, 1.0f, curve + energyOffset); }

    void setCurve (float c, juce::NotificationType n = juce::sendNotification)
    {
        const float v = juce::jlimit (-1.0f, 1.0f, c);
        if (std::abs (v - curve) < 1.0e-4f) return;
        curve = v;
        repaint();
        if (n == juce::sendNotification && onChange) onChange (curve);
    }
    float getCurve() const noexcept { return curve; }

    void paint (juce::Graphics& g) override
    {
        auto b = getLocalBounds().reduced (2).toFloat();
        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xFF141414));
        g.fillRoundedRectangle (b, 3.0f);

        // Grid + the linear diagonal, so the bend is readable against a
        // reference rather than as an abstract line.
        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xFF2E2E2E));
        for (int i = 1; i < 4; ++i)
        {
            const float t = (float) i / 4.0f;
            g.drawHorizontalLine ((int) (b.getY() + t * b.getHeight()), b.getX(), b.getRight());
            g.drawVerticalLine   ((int) (b.getX() + t * b.getWidth()),  b.getY(), b.getBottom());
        }
        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xFF3A3A3A));
        g.drawLine (b.getX(), b.getBottom(), b.getRight(), b.getY(), 1.0f);

        juce::Path path;
        const int steps = juce::jmax (16, (int) b.getWidth());
        for (int i = 0; i <= steps; ++i)
        {
            const float x = (float) i / (float) steps;
            const float y = VelCurve::shape (x, effectiveCurve());
            const float px = b.getX() + x * b.getWidth();
            const float py = b.getBottom() - y * b.getHeight();
            if (i == 0) path.startNewSubPath (px, py); else path.lineTo (px, py);
        }
        g.setColour (juce::Colour (Theme::Gold::kAccent));
        g.strokePath (path, juce::PathStrokeType (2.0f));

        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xFFC2C2C2));
        g.setFont (juce::Font (juce::FontOptions (11.0f)));
        g.drawText (label(), getLocalBounds().removeFromBottom (14),
                    juce::Justification::centred);
    }

    void mouseDown (const juce::MouseEvent& e) override { dragFrom = curve; lastY = e.position.y; }

    void mouseDrag (const juce::MouseEvent& e) override
    {
        const float dy = lastY - e.position.y;          // up = harder
        setCurve (dragFrom + dy / juce::jmax (40.0f, (float) getHeight()));
    }
    void mouseDoubleClick (const juce::MouseEvent&) override { setCurve (0.0f); }

private:
    /** Reads the EFFECTIVE curve, and says so when ENERGY is moving it - a
        number that silently disagrees with the slot's stored value would be the
        worst of both designs. */
    juce::String label() const
    {
        const float e = effectiveCurve();
        juce::String s;

        if (std::abs (e) < 0.02f) s = "LINEAR";
        else s = (e < 0.0f ? "SOFT " : "HARD ")
               + juce::String ((int) std::lround (std::abs (e) * 100.0f));

        if (std::abs (energyOffset) >= 0.005f)
            s += " (ENERGY " + juce::String (energyOffset > 0.0f ? "+" : "")
               + juce::String ((int) std::lround (energyOffset * 100.0f)) + ")";

        return s;
    }

    float curve = 0.0f, dragFrom = 0.0f, lastY = 0.0f;
    float energyOffset = 0.0f;
};


class GoldSlider : public juce::Component
{
public:
    // ── Locked geometry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    static constexpr float kTrackWidth     = 10.0f;
    static constexpr float kOuterRadius    = 20.0f;   // 40 px black handle (4 × track width)
    static constexpr float kInnerRadius    = 7.0f;    // 14 px bronze inner dot
    static constexpr float kValueFont      = 14.0f;
    static constexpr float kLabelFont      = 16.0f;
    static constexpr float kValueAreaH     = 20.0f;
    static constexpr float kLabelAreaH     = 24.0f;
    static constexpr float kHandleClearance = 2.0f;   // gap between handle and value/label areas
    static constexpr float kVerticalReserved =
        kValueAreaH + kLabelAreaH + 2.0f * kOuterRadius + 2.0f * kHandleClearance;
    // Horizontal mode reserves only handle margin at each end; value text /
    // label live in dedicated top / bottom bands and don't consume track length.
    static constexpr float kHorizontalReserved =
        2.0f * kOuterRadius + 2.0f * kHandleClearance;

    std::function<void(float)> onChange;

    /** Natura: host gesture brackets, so automation records a drag as one move. */
    std::function<void()> onDragStart, onDragEnd;

    /** Optional readout override — takes the raw slider value and returns what
        to print.  See valueText. */
    std::function<juce::String(float)> displayFn;

    GoldSlider(const juce::String& lbl, float minV, float maxV, float defV,
               const juce::String& unitStr_ = "")
        : label(lbl), unit(unitStr_), minVal(minV), maxVal(maxV), value(defV), defVal(defV) {}

    /** Set a snap step (e.g. 1.0f for integer 0..100 sliders).  step <= 0
        means continuous (default).  Existing value is re-quantised. */
    void setStep(float s)
    {
        step = juce::jmax(0.0f, s);
        if (step > 0.0f) value = quantise(value);
        repaint();
    }
    float getStep() const { return step; }

    /** Switch to horizontal track layout (default is vertical).  Used by the
        portamento and octave sliders in SynthesisPanel where the host frame
        is short and wide and 7 discrete octave steps need horizontal room to
        be hit-targetable. */
    void setHorizontal (bool h) noexcept { horizontal = h; repaint(); }
    bool isHorizontal() const noexcept   { return horizontal; }

    void setValue(float v, bool notify = false)
    {
        const float clamped = juce::jlimit(minVal, maxVal, v);
        const float snapped = (step > 0.0f) ? quantise(clamped) : clamped;
        if (snapped == value && ! notify) return;
        value = snapped;
        repaint();
        if (notify && onChange) onChange(value);
    }
    float getValue() const { return value; }

    void paint(juce::Graphics& g) override
    {
        if (horizontal) paintHorizontal(g);
        else            paintVertical  (g);
    }

    void mouseDown(const juce::MouseEvent& e) override
    {
        dragX = e.x;
        dragY = e.y;
        dragVal = value;
        setMouseCursor(horizontal ? juce::MouseCursor::LeftRightResizeCursor
                                  : juce::MouseCursor::UpDownResizeCursor);
        if (! e.mods.isRightButtonDown() && onDragStart) { dragging = true; onDragStart(); }
    }

    void mouseDrag(const juce::MouseEvent& e) override
    {
        if (e.mods.isRightButtonDown()) return;      // right button = reset only
        if (horizontal)
        {
            const float trkW = (float) getWidth() - kHorizontalReserved;
            if (trkW > 0.0f)
                setValue(dragVal + ((float)(e.x - dragX) / trkW) * (maxVal - minVal), true);
        }
        else
        {
            const float trkH = (float) getHeight() - kVerticalReserved;
            if (trkH > 0.0f)
                setValue(dragVal + ((float)(dragY - e.y) / trkH) * (maxVal - minVal), true);
        }
    }

    void mouseUp(const juce::MouseEvent&) override
    {
        setMouseCursor(juce::MouseCursor::NormalCursor);
        if (dragging) { dragging = false; if (onDragEnd) onDragEnd(); }
    }

    //==========================================================================
    // DOUBLE-CLICK GESTURES
    //
    //   RIGHT double-click -> reset to default.  (Moved here from the left
    //                         button so the left one is free.)
    //   LEFT  double-click -> onLeftDoubleClick, if the owner set one.  Only the
    //                         GAIN sliders do; everywhere else it is inert.
    //
    // A right DRAG no longer moves the value either — otherwise a slightly
    // sloppy right double-click would nudge the very number it is resetting.
    //==========================================================================
    std::function<void()> onLeftDoubleClick;

    void mouseDoubleClick(const juce::MouseEvent& e) override
    {
        if (e.mods.isRightButtonDown())
        {
            if (onDragStart) onDragStart();
            setValue(defVal, true);
            if (onDragEnd) onDragEnd();
            return;
        }
        if (onLeftDoubleClick) onLeftDoubleClick();
    }

private:
    void paintVertical(juce::Graphics& g)
    {
        const float W = (float) getWidth();
        const float H = (float) getHeight();
        if (W < 4.0f || H < 8.0f) return;

        const float cx = W * 0.5f;
        const float trkX = cx - kTrackWidth * 0.5f;
        const float trkT = kValueAreaH + kOuterRadius + kHandleClearance;
        const float trkB = H - kLabelAreaH - kOuterRadius - kHandleClearance;
        const float trkH = juce::jmax(8.0f, trkB - trkT);

        // ── Medium-gray rounded backdrop (one card per slider) ────────────────
        {
            const float inset  = 2.0f;
            const float corner = 6.0f;
            juce::Rectangle<float> bg(inset, inset, W - inset * 2.0f, H - inset * 2.0f);

            juce::ColourGradient bgGrad(juce::Colour(0xFF454545), bg.getX(), bg.getY(),
                                        juce::Colour(0xFF323232), bg.getX(), bg.getBottom(), false);
            g.setGradientFill(bgGrad);
            g.fillRoundedRectangle(bg, corner);

            g.setColour(juce::Colours::black.withAlpha(0.55f));
            g.drawRoundedRectangle(bg, corner, 1.0f);
        }

        // ── Recessed "valley" railway ─────────────────────────────────────────
        // Symmetric cross-section: the two outer edges are lighter (light from
        // above catches the lips of the groove), and the centre is darkest
        // (the floor of the U-shaped valley sits in shadow). This reads as a
        // channel cut INTO the panel, the opposite of a raised cylinder.
        juce::ColourGradient trackGrad(juce::Colour(0xFF2E2E2E), trkX - 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                       juce::Colour(0xFF2E2E2E), trkX + kTrackWidth + 1.0f, 0.0f, false);
        trackGrad.addColour(0.5, juce::Colour(0xFF020202));
        g.setGradientFill(trackGrad);
        g.fillRoundedRectangle(trkX, trkT, kTrackWidth, trkH, kTrackWidth * 0.5f);

        // Thin black outline reads as the groove's hard edge against the panel
        g.setColour(juce::Colour(0xFF000000).withAlpha(0.85f));
        g.drawRoundedRectangle(trkX + 0.5f, trkT + 0.5f,
                               kTrackWidth - 1.0f, trkH - 1.0f, kTrackWidth * 0.5f - 0.5f, 0.8f);

        // ── Bronze fill from handle position down ─────────────────────────────
        const float norm   = (maxVal > minVal) ? (value - minVal) / (maxVal - minVal) : 0.0f;
        const float thumbY = trkB - norm * trkH;

        juce::Path pillPath;
        pillPath.addRoundedRectangle(trkX, trkT, kTrackWidth, trkH, kTrackWidth * 0.5f);
        g.saveState();
        g.reduceClipRegion(pillPath);

        juce::ColourGradient bronzeGrad(juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentLight), trkX - 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                        juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentDark), trkX + kTrackWidth + 1.0f, 0.0f, false);
        bronzeGrad.addColour(0.5, juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccent));
        g.setGradientFill(bronzeGrad);
        g.fillRect(juce::Rectangle<float>(trkX, thumbY, kTrackWidth, trkB - thumbY));
        g.restoreState();

        // ── Outer BLACK gradient handle (40 px diameter) ──────────────────────
        // Radial highlight in the upper-left, falling off to black at the rim.
        juce::ColourGradient outerGrad(juce::Colour(0xFF6A6A6A),
                                       cx - kOuterRadius * 0.4f,
                                       thumbY - kOuterRadius * 0.4f,
                                       juce::Colour(0xFF000000),
                                       cx + kOuterRadius,
                                       thumbY + kOuterRadius, true);
        outerGrad.addColour(0.45, juce::Colour(0xFF2E2E2E));
        outerGrad.addColour(0.85, juce::Colour(0xFF0A0A0A));
        g.setGradientFill(outerGrad);
        g.fillEllipse(cx - kOuterRadius, thumbY - kOuterRadius,
                      kOuterRadius * 2.0f, kOuterRadius * 2.0f);

        // Subtle bevel rim + dark inset
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white.withAlpha(0.22f));
        g.drawEllipse(cx - kOuterRadius + 0.6f, thumbY - kOuterRadius + 0.6f,
                      kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 1.2f, kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 1.2f, 0.9f);
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::black.withAlpha(0.85f));
        g.drawEllipse(cx - kOuterRadius + 0.2f, thumbY - kOuterRadius + 0.2f,
                      kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, 0.8f);

        // ── Inner BRONZE circle (the "dot") ───────────────────────────────────
        juce::ColourGradient innerGrad(juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentLight),
                                       cx - kInnerRadius * 0.35f,
                                       thumbY - kInnerRadius * 0.35f,
                                       juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentGradDk),
                                       cx + kInnerRadius,
                                       thumbY + kInnerRadius, true);
        innerGrad.addColour(0.5, juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentGrad));
        g.setGradientFill(innerGrad);
        g.fillEllipse(cx - kInnerRadius, thumbY - kInnerRadius,
                      kInnerRadius * 2.0f, kInnerRadius * 2.0f);

        // Thin dark rim around the bronze dot so it pops against the black handle
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::black.withAlpha(0.7f));
        g.drawEllipse(cx - kInnerRadius + 0.2f, thumbY - kInnerRadius + 0.2f,
                      kInnerRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, kInnerRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, 0.7f);

        // ── Value text (top) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
        g.setFont(juce::Font(juce::FontOptions(kValueFont)));
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white.withAlpha(0.90f));
        g.drawFittedText(formatVal(), 0, 2, (int) W, (int)(kValueAreaH - 2),
                         juce::Justification::centred, 1, 0.6f);

        // ── Label (bottom) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
        g.setFont(juce::Font(juce::FontOptions(kLabelFont, juce::Font::bold)));
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white.withAlpha(0.90f));
        g.drawFittedText(label, 0, (int)(H - kLabelAreaH), (int) W, (int) kLabelAreaH,
                         juce::Justification::centred, 1, 0.5f);
    }

    // ── Horizontal mode ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Mirrors paintVertical: same value-top / label-bottom bands, same handle
    // sizes, same bronze + black palette.  Only difference is that the track
    // runs LEFT to RIGHT through the middle of the component, the bronze fill
    // grows from the left edge toward the handle, and the U-channel gradient
    // runs perpendicular (top→middle→bottom) so the recessed cross-section
    // reads the same way.
    void paintHorizontal(juce::Graphics& g)
    {
        const float W = (float) getWidth();
        const float H = (float) getHeight();
        if (W < 8.0f || H < 4.0f) return;

        // The middle band sits between the value text (top) and label (bottom).
        const float cy   = kValueAreaH + kOuterRadius + kHandleClearance;
        const float trkY = cy - kTrackWidth * 0.5f;
        const float trkL = kOuterRadius + kHandleClearance;
        const float trkR = W - kOuterRadius - kHandleClearance;
        const float trkW = juce::jmax(8.0f, trkR - trkL);

        // Background card
        {
            const float inset  = 2.0f;
            const float corner = 6.0f;
            juce::Rectangle<float> bg(inset, inset, W - inset * 2.0f, H - inset * 2.0f);

            juce::ColourGradient bgGrad(juce::Colour(0xFF454545), bg.getX(), bg.getY(),
                                        juce::Colour(0xFF323232), bg.getX(), bg.getBottom(), false);
            g.setGradientFill(bgGrad);
            g.fillRoundedRectangle(bg, corner);

            g.setColour(juce::Colours::black.withAlpha(0.55f));
            g.drawRoundedRectangle(bg, corner, 1.0f);
        }

        // Recessed "valley" track — gradient runs vertically across the track
        // (light at top/bottom edges, dark at centre) for the same U-channel
        // read as the vertical case.
        juce::ColourGradient trackGrad(juce::Colour(0xFF2E2E2E), 0.0f, trkY - 1.0f,
                                       juce::Colour(0xFF2E2E2E), 0.0f, trkY + kTrackWidth + 1.0f, false);
        trackGrad.addColour(0.5, juce::Colour(0xFF020202));
        g.setGradientFill(trackGrad);
        g.fillRoundedRectangle(trkL, trkY, trkW, kTrackWidth, kTrackWidth * 0.5f);

        g.setColour(juce::Colour(0xFF000000).withAlpha(0.85f));
        g.drawRoundedRectangle(trkL + 0.5f, trkY + 0.5f,
                               trkW - 1.0f, kTrackWidth - 1.0f, kTrackWidth * 0.5f - 0.5f, 0.8f);

        // Bronze fill from LEFT edge to handle x
        const float norm   = (maxVal > minVal) ? (value - minVal) / (maxVal - minVal) : 0.0f;
        const float thumbX = trkL + norm * trkW;

        juce::Path pillPath;
        pillPath.addRoundedRectangle(trkL, trkY, trkW, kTrackWidth, kTrackWidth * 0.5f);
        g.saveState();
        g.reduceClipRegion(pillPath);

        juce::ColourGradient bronzeGrad(juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentLight), 0.0f, trkY - 1.0f,
                                        juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentDark), 0.0f, trkY + kTrackWidth + 1.0f, false);
        bronzeGrad.addColour(0.5, juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccent));
        g.setGradientFill(bronzeGrad);
        g.fillRect(juce::Rectangle<float>(trkL, trkY, thumbX - trkL, kTrackWidth));
        g.restoreState();

        // Outer BLACK handle centred at (thumbX, cy)
        juce::ColourGradient outerGrad(juce::Colour(0xFF6A6A6A),
                                       thumbX - kOuterRadius * 0.4f,
                                       cy     - kOuterRadius * 0.4f,
                                       juce::Colour(0xFF000000),
                                       thumbX + kOuterRadius,
                                       cy     + kOuterRadius, true);
        outerGrad.addColour(0.45, juce::Colour(0xFF2E2E2E));
        outerGrad.addColour(0.85, juce::Colour(0xFF0A0A0A));
        g.setGradientFill(outerGrad);
        g.fillEllipse(thumbX - kOuterRadius, cy - kOuterRadius,
                      kOuterRadius * 2.0f, kOuterRadius * 2.0f);

        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white.withAlpha(0.22f));
        g.drawEllipse(thumbX - kOuterRadius + 0.6f, cy - kOuterRadius + 0.6f,
                      kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 1.2f, kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 1.2f, 0.9f);
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::black.withAlpha(0.85f));
        g.drawEllipse(thumbX - kOuterRadius + 0.2f, cy - kOuterRadius + 0.2f,
                      kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, kOuterRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, 0.8f);

        // Inner BRONZE dot
        juce::ColourGradient innerGrad(juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentLight),
                                       thumbX - kInnerRadius * 0.35f,
                                       cy     - kInnerRadius * 0.35f,
                                       juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentGradDk),
                                       thumbX + kInnerRadius,
                                       cy     + kInnerRadius, true);
        innerGrad.addColour(0.5, juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccentGrad));
        g.setGradientFill(innerGrad);
        g.fillEllipse(thumbX - kInnerRadius, cy - kInnerRadius,
                      kInnerRadius * 2.0f, kInnerRadius * 2.0f);

        g.setColour(juce::Colours::black.withAlpha(0.7f));
        g.drawEllipse(thumbX - kInnerRadius + 0.2f, cy - kInnerRadius + 0.2f,
                      kInnerRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, kInnerRadius * 2.0f - 0.4f, 0.7f);

        // Value text (top), label (bottom) — same bands as the vertical layout.
        g.setFont(juce::Font(juce::FontOptions(kValueFont)));
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white.withAlpha(0.90f));
        g.drawFittedText(formatVal(), 0, 2, (int) W, (int)(kValueAreaH - 2),
                         juce::Justification::centred, 1, 0.6f);

        g.setFont(juce::Font(juce::FontOptions(kLabelFont, juce::Font::bold)));
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white.withAlpha(0.90f));
        g.drawFittedText(label, 0, (int)(H - kLabelAreaH), (int) W, (int) kLabelAreaH,
                         juce::Justification::centred, 1, 0.5f);
    }

    juce::String formatVal() const
    {
        // Integer-valued sliders (step == 1) display without decimals — used
        // for the 0..100 normalised sliders in DrumsPopup.
        // Natura: a readout override always wins (note names, choice names,
        // times), the integer shortcut is only for plain stepped numbers.
        if (displayFn) return displayFn (value);

        if (step >= 1.0f && unit.isEmpty())
            return juce::String((int) std::round(value));

        // A knob whose VALUE is not what it MEANS supplies its own readout.
        //
        // A/D/R carry 0..100 because the drag is linear between min and max
        // while their real scale is exponential, so the number under the knob
        // would otherwise be a POSITION, not a time.  That is exactly how a
        // release of "70" changed from 2.1 s to 629 ms in a rebuild with
        // nothing on screen disagreeing.  Show the time and it cannot recur.
        if (displayFn) return displayFn (value);

        if (unit == "s")   return value < 1.0f ? juce::String((int)(value*1000)) + "ms"
                                               : juce::String(value, 1) + "s";
        if (unit == "ms")  return juce::String((int)value) + "ms";
        if (unit == "Hz")  return juce::String(value, 2) + "Hz";
        if (unit == "dB")  return juce::String(value, 1) + "dB";
        if (unit == "st")  return juce::String(value, 1) + "st";
        if (unit == "BPM") return juce::String((int)value) + " BPM";
        return juce::String(value, 2) + unit;
    }

    float quantise(float v) const
    {
        if (step <= 0.0f) return v;
        const float n = std::round((v - minVal) / step);
        return juce::jlimit(minVal, maxVal, minVal + n * step);
    }

    juce::String label, unit;
    float minVal, maxVal, value, defVal;
    float step = 0.0f;     // 0 = continuous
    bool  horizontal = false;
    int   dragX = 0;
    int   dragY = 0;
    float dragVal = 0.f;
    bool  dragging = false;
};


namespace InstrEditStyle
{
    //==========================================================================
    // PANEL LABEL COLOUR — #C2C2C2, and the ONE place it is decided.
    //
    // The left panel's captions and separator lines used to be pure #FFFFFF,
    // while the two macro triggers beside them rendered at #C2C2C2 (a plain
    // TextButton goes through the LookAndFeel, which does not draw at full
    // white).  Measured off a screenshot, that is a 61-unit gap on every
    // channel — enough that the panel read as two different families of control
    // sitting in one frame.
    //
    // Everything on that panel now uses this.  Pure white stays where it earns
    // its contrast: the amber-lit states, the LED speculars, and the tab row.
    //==========================================================================
    inline const juce::Colour kPanelLabel { 0xFFC2C2C2 };

    constexpr float kFrameCorner    = 20.0f;
    constexpr int   kFrameSidePad   = 14;
    constexpr int   kFrameTopPad    = 8;
    constexpr int   kFrameTitleH    = 22;
    constexpr int   kFrameTitleGap  = 6;
    constexpr int   kFrameBottomPad = 14;

    inline void paintComponentFrame(juce::Graphics& g, juce::Rectangle<int> bounds,
                                    const juce::String& title)
    {
        const auto fb = bounds.toFloat();

        g.setColour(juce::Colour(0xFF1A1A1A));
        g.fillRoundedRectangle(fb, kFrameCorner);

        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white);
        g.drawRoundedRectangle(fb.reduced(0.5f), kFrameCorner, 1.0f);

        if (title.isNotEmpty())
        {
            g.setColour(juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccent));
            g.setFont(juce::Font(juce::FontOptions(15.0f, juce::Font::bold)));
            g.drawFittedText(title,
                             bounds.getX() + 12, bounds.getY() + kFrameTopPad,
                             bounds.getWidth() - 24, kFrameTitleH,
                             juce::Justification::centred, 1);
        }
    }

    inline juce::Rectangle<int> componentFrameContent(juce::Rectangle<int> bounds)
    {
        const int top = kFrameTopPad + kFrameTitleH + kFrameTitleGap;
        return { bounds.getX() + kFrameSidePad,
                 bounds.getY() + top,
                 bounds.getWidth()  - kFrameSidePad * 2,
                 bounds.getHeight() - top - kFrameBottomPad };
    }

    inline void styleSquareButton(juce::TextButton& b, bool active)
    {
        const auto fill = active ? juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccent) : juce::Colour(0xFF2A2A2A);

        // BOTH ids, and that is the whole fix for "my toggles never go orange".
        // LookAndFeel_V4::drawButtonBackground looks up buttonOnColourId when the
        // button's TOGGLE STATE is set and buttonColourId when it is not — so a
        // plain button styled here went amber correctly, while any button with
        // setClickingTogglesState(true) fell through to the untouched default the
        // moment it was switched on.
        b.setColour(juce::TextButton::buttonColourId,   fill);
        b.setColour(juce::TextButton::buttonOnColourId, fill);
        // Black on the amber fill, white on the inert one - the label has to
        // read against whichever background it just got.
        const auto text = active ? juce::Colours::black : juce::Colours::white;
        b.setColour(juce::TextButton::textColourOffId, text);
        b.setColour(juce::TextButton::textColourOnId,  text);
    }

    inline void drawSectionHeader(juce::Graphics& g, const juce::String& label,
                                  int x, int y, int w, int h = 14)
    {
        g.setColour(juce::Colour(Theme::Gold::kAccent));
        g.setFont(juce::Font(juce::FontOptions((float) juce::jmin(h - 2, 11), juce::Font::bold)));
        g.drawText(label, x, y, w, h, juce::Justification::centred, false);
    }
    inline void drawDivider(juce::Graphics& g, int x, int yTop, int yBot)
    {
        g.setColour(juce::Colours::white.withAlpha(0.06f));
        g.drawVerticalLine(x, (float) yTop, (float) yBot);
    }
}

// C:\workspace\SONIFY PLUGIN natura\src\ModelBase.h
#pragma once
//==============================================================================
//  ModelBase.h  -  what every archetype model receives and how it is driven.
//
//  A model is the SOUND SOURCE of a voice.  The voice's own chain (body,
//  character, the synthesis filter and envelopes, the LFOs) shapes what comes
//  out of it, exactly like an ordinary synthesizer shapes an oscillator.
//
//  The voice hands a model a ModelIn once per control block (16 samples):
//  pitch, breath / bow pressure, the shared section values and the model's own
//  archetype-specific values, all normalised 0..1.  Pure C++, no JUCE.
//==============================================================================
#include "ModelDsp.h"
#include "OscEngine.h"

namespace natura
{
    /** How the voice turns dynamics (velocity / breath / expression) into the
        model's pressure input and its output level. */
    enum class Dynamics
    {
        Physical,   // pressure = env, dyn passed through: each model keeps its own
                    // physics inside the window where it speaks; level * (0.25 + 0.75 dyn)
        Direct,     // pressure = env * dyn (the model shapes its own response)
        Swell,      // pressure = env, level * dyn (organs: the swell pedal)
        Struck      // velocity strikes it; a continuous source rides the level
    };

    /** How a note is set going - articulations can change it. */
    enum class Excite { Normal = 0, Pluck, Strike };

    /** Brass mutes (Lip Reed archetype, also the Mute articulations). */
    enum class Mute { Open = 0, Straight, Cup, Harmon, Wah };

    constexpr int kMaxSpec = 16;

    struct ModelIn
    {
        // pitch and dynamics ---------------------------------------------------
        float freq     = 440.0f;   // Hz, everything included (bend, glide, vibrato)
        float pressure = 0.0f;     // sustained drive envelope 0..1 (breath, bow, bellows)
        float dyn      = 1.0f;     // 0..1 the player's dynamics (velocity, breath CC, expression)
        float velocity = 0.8f;     // 0..1 after the velocity curve
        int   note     = 60;
        std::uint32_t seed = 0;    // per note and unison unit: no two strikes alike

        // EXCITER --------------------------------------------------------------
        float strength  = 0.5f;
        float hardness  = 0.5f;
        float noise     = 0.2f;
        float transient = 0.5f;

        // RESONATOR ------------------------------------------------------------
        float decay    = 0.5f;
        float damping  = 0.5f;
        float inharm   = 0.2f;
        float oddEven  = 0.5f;

        // archetype-specific, in the model's own order --------------------------
        float spec[kMaxSpec] = {};

        // performance ------------------------------------------------------------
        float  bright   = 0.0f;    // -1..1 offset from mod wheel / aftertouch / VAR
        float  dampAdd  = 0.0f;    // 0..1 articulation damping (palm mute, dead stroke)
        float  decayMul = 1.0f;    // articulation decay scale
        float  pedal    = 0.0f;    // 0..1 damper lift (sustain pedal, half pedal)
        float  soft     = 0.0f;    // 0..1 una corda / soft pedal
        float  growl    = 0.0f;    // 0..1 growl / flutter roughness on the drive
        float  wah      = 0.5f;    // 0..1 wah mute position
        Excite excite   = Excite::Normal;
        Mute   mute     = Mute::Open;
        int    stateOffset = 0;    // free-reed register shift
        bool   percTrigger = true; // tonewheel percussion is single-trigger
        bool   harmonic = false;   // natural harmonic (plucked: excite at the node)
        bool   released = false;

        const oscengine::Params* osc = nullptr;   // SYNTH archetype settings
    };

    class ModelBase
    {
    public:
        virtual ~ModelBase() = default;

        virtual void prepare (double sampleRate) = 0;
        virtual void reset() = 0;

        /** A new note.  legato: the same voice carries on (mono slur) - keep the
            resonator ringing, only move the pitch and, where it makes sense,
            excite softly. */
        virtual void start (const ModelIn& in, bool legato) = 0;

        /** Key up (after the sustain pedal has been taken into account). */
        virtual void release (const ModelIn& in) = 0;

        /** n samples, n <= 64. */
        virtual void render (const ModelIn& in, float* out, int n) = 0;

        /** Sustained-drive models (bow, breath, bellows) need the voice's
            pressure envelope; decaying models (struck, plucked) do not. */
        virtual bool isSustained() const = 0;

        virtual Dynamics dynamics() const = 0;

    protected:
        double sr = 48000.0;
    };
}

// C:\workspace\SONIFY PLUGIN natura\src\ModelDsp.h
#pragma once
//==============================================================================
//  ModelDsp.h  -  the small building blocks every Natura model is made of.
//
//  Pure C++, no JUCE: the audio thread runs it, and the offline test harness
//  renders it from the same code.  Nothing here allocates after prepare().
//==============================================================================
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <complex>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

namespace natura::dsp
{
    constexpr double kPi    = 3.14159265358979323846;
    constexpr double kTwoPi = 6.28318530717958647692;

    template <typename T> inline T clampv (T v, T lo, T hi) { return v < lo ? lo : (v > hi ? hi : v); }
    inline float lerp (float a, float b, float t) { return a + (b - a) * t; }
    inline float dbToGain (float db) { return std::pow (10.0f, db * 0.05f); }

    /** Loop gain per period that gives a T60 of t60 seconds at f0. */
    inline float loopGainForT60 (float t60, float f0)
    {
        t60 = std::max (0.005f, t60);
        f0  = std::max (1.0f, f0);
        return std::pow (10.0f, -3.0f / (t60 * f0));
    }

    /** Per-sample multiplier that gives a T60 of t60 seconds. */
    inline float sampleGainForT60 (float t60, double sr)
    {
        t60 = std::max (0.001f, t60);
        return (float) std::pow (10.0, -3.0 / ((double) t60 * sr));
    }

    //==========================================================================
    //  Fast white noise, -1..1
    //==========================================================================
    struct Noise
    {
        std::uint32_t s = 0x12345678u;
        void seed (std::uint32_t v) { s = v ? v : 0x9E3779B9u; }
        float next()
        {
            s ^= s << 13; s ^= s >> 17; s ^= s << 5;
            return (float) (std::int32_t) s * (1.0f / 2147483648.0f);
        }
        float unit() { return 0.5f * (next() + 1.0f); }   // 0..1
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  Fractional delay line, 4-point Lagrange read.
    //  tap(d): the sample written d samples ago (d = 1 is the last write).
    //==========================================================================
    struct FracDelay
    {
        std::vector<float> buf;
        int mask = 0, w = 0;

        void prepare (int maxSamples)
        {
            int n = 16;
            while (n < maxSamples + 8) n <<= 1;
            buf.assign ((size_t) n, 0.0f);
            mask = n - 1;
            w = 0;
        }
        void clear() { std::fill (buf.begin(), buf.end(), 0.0f); }
        int  capacity() const { return mask - 6; }

        void write (float x) { buf[(size_t) w] = x; w = (w + 1) & mask; }

        float at (int d) const { return buf[(size_t) ((w - d) & mask)]; }

        float tap (float d) const
        {
            d = clampv (d, 2.0f, (float) capacity());
            const int   i = (int) d;
            const float t = d - (float) i + 1.0f;          // 1 .. 2
            const float x0 = at (i - 1), x1 = at (i), x2 = at (i + 1), x3 = at (i + 2);
            const float tm1 = t - 1.0f, tm2 = t - 2.0f, tm3 = t - 3.0f;
            const float h0 = -tm1 * tm2 * tm3 * (1.0f / 6.0f);
            const float h1 =  t   * tm2 * tm3 * 0.5f;
            const float h2 = -t   * tm1 * tm3 * 0.5f;
            const float h3 =  t   * tm1 * tm2 * (1.0f / 6.0f);
            return h0 * x0 + h1 * x1 + h2 * x2 + h3 * x3;
        }

        /** |H| of the Lagrange read at w for delay d.  In a loop that runs
            thousands of periods a second, even 0.5% loss per pass is fatal to
            the decay, so loop gains are divided by this. */
        static float lagrangeMag (float d, double w)
        {
            const int   i = (int) std::max (2.0f, d);
            const float t = std::max (2.0f, d) - (float) i + 1.0f;
            const float tm1 = t - 1.0f, tm2 = t - 2.0f, tm3 = t - 3.0f;
            const float h[4] = { -tm1 * tm2 * tm3 * (1.0f / 6.0f), t * tm2 * tm3 * 0.5f,
                                 -t * tm1 * tm3 * 0.5f, t * tm1 * tm2 * (1.0f / 6.0f) };
            std::complex<double> acc (0.0, 0.0);
            for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k) acc += (double) h[k] * std::polar (1.0, -w * (double) k);
            return (float) std::abs (acc);
        }

        /** Linear read, used where Lagrange's slight HF lift is unwanted. */
        float tapLin (float d) const
        {
            d = clampv (d, 1.0f, (float) capacity());
            const int   i = (int) d;
            const float f = d - (float) i;
            return at (i) + f * (at (i + 1) - at (i));
        }
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  One-pole low-pass  y = (1-a) x + a y1   (a 0..1, higher = darker)
    //==========================================================================
    struct OnePoleLP
    {
        float a = 0.0f, y = 0.0f;
        void  reset() { y = 0.0f; }
        void  setCutoff (double hz, double sr) { a = (float) std::exp (-kTwoPi * std::max (1.0, hz) / sr); }
        float process (float x) { y = (1.0f - a) * x + a * y; return y; }

        /** Phase delay in samples of the filter at w (radians/sample). */
        static float phaseDelay (float a, double w)
        {
            if (w <= 1.0e-9) return a / (1.0f - a);
            return (float) (std::atan2 ((double) a * std::sin (w), 1.0 - (double) a * std::cos (w)) / w);
        }
        static float magnitude (float a, double w)
        {
            const std::complex<double> z = std::polar (1.0, -w);
            return (float) std::abs ((1.0 - a) / (1.0 - (double) a * z));
        }
    };

    struct OnePoleHP
    {
        OnePoleLP lp;
        void  reset() { lp.reset(); }
        void  setCutoff (double hz, double sr) { lp.setCutoff (hz, sr); }
        float process (float x) { return x - lp.process (x); }
    };

    struct DCBlocker
    {
        float x1 = 0.0f, y1 = 0.0f, r = 0.995f;
        void  prepare (double sr, double hz = 20.0) { r = (float) (1.0 - kTwoPi * hz / sr); }
        void  reset() { x1 = y1 = 0.0f; }
        float process (float x) { const float y = x - x1 + r * y1; x1 = x; y1 = y; return y; }

        /** Phase delay in samples at w - NEGATIVE (a DC blocker leads), so a
            loop that carries one must be made that much LONGER. */
        static float phaseDelay (float r, double w)
        {
            const std::complex<double> z = std::polar (1.0, -w);
            const std::complex<double> h = (1.0 - z) / (1.0 - (double) r * z);
            return (float) (-std::arg (h) / std::max (1.0e-9, w));
        }
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  First-order allpass  H = (c + z^-1) / (1 + c z^-1)
    //==========================================================================
    struct Allpass1
    {
        float c = 0.0f, x1 = 0.0f, y1 = 0.0f;
        void  reset() { x1 = y1 = 0.0f; }
        float process (float x) { const float y = c * x + x1 - c * y1; x1 = x; y1 = y; return y; }

        static float phaseDelay (float c, double w)
        {
            if (w <= 1.0e-9) return (1.0f - c) / (1.0f + c);
            const std::complex<double> z = std::polar (1.0, -w);
            const std::complex<double> h = ((double) c + z) / (1.0 + (double) c * z);
            double ph = -std::arg (h);
            if (ph < 0.0) ph += kTwoPi;
            return (float) (ph / w);
        }
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  RBJ biquad, transposed direct form II
    //==========================================================================
    struct Biquad
    {
        float b0 = 1, b1 = 0, b2 = 0, a1 = 0, a2 = 0, z1 = 0, z2 = 0;

        void  reset() { z1 = z2 = 0.0f; }
        float process (float x)
        {
            const float y = b0 * x + z1;
            z1 = b1 * x - a1 * y + z2;
            z2 = b2 * x - a2 * y;
            return y;
        }

        void set (double nb0, double nb1, double nb2, double na0, double na1, double na2)
        {
            b0 = (float) (nb0 / na0); b1 = (float) (nb1 / na0); b2 = (float) (nb2 / na0);
            a1 = (float) (na1 / na0); a2 = (float) (na2 / na0);
        }

        static double w0 (double hz, double sr) { return kTwoPi * clampv (hz, 10.0, sr * 0.49) / sr; }

        void lowpass (double hz, double q, double sr)
        {
            const double w = w0 (hz, sr), cw = std::cos (w), al = std::sin (w) / (2.0 * q);
            set ((1 - cw) / 2, 1 - cw, (1 - cw) / 2, 1 + al, -2 * cw, 1 - al);
        }
        void highpass (double hz, double q, double sr)
        {
            const double w = w0 (hz, sr), cw = std::cos (w), al = std::sin (w) / (2.0 * q);
            set ((1 + cw) / 2, -(1 + cw), (1 + cw) / 2, 1 + al, -2 * cw, 1 - al);
        }
        void bandpass (double hz, double q, double sr)        // 0 dB peak
        {
            const double w = w0 (hz, sr), cw = std::cos (w), al = std::sin (w) / (2.0 * q);
            set (al, 0, -al, 1 + al, -2 * cw, 1 - al);
        }
        void peak (double hz, double q, double db, double sr)
        {
            const double A = std::pow (10.0, db / 40.0);
            const double w = w0 (hz, sr), cw = std::cos (w), al = std::sin (w) / (2.0 * q);
            set (1 + al * A, -2 * cw, 1 - al * A, 1 + al / A, -2 * cw, 1 - al / A);
        }
        void lowShelf (double hz, double db, double sr)
        {
            const double A = std::pow (10.0, db / 40.0);
            const double w = w0 (hz, sr), cw = std::cos (w), sw = std::sin (w);
            const double al = sw / 2.0 * std::sqrt (2.0), sa = 2.0 * std::sqrt (A) * al;
            set (A * ((A + 1) - (A - 1) * cw + sa), 2 * A * ((A - 1) - (A + 1) * cw), A * ((A + 1) - (A - 1) * cw - sa),
                 (A + 1) + (A - 1) * cw + sa, -2 * ((A - 1) + (A + 1) * cw), (A + 1) + (A - 1) * cw - sa);
        }
        void highShelf (double hz, double db, double sr)
        {
            const double A = std::pow (10.0, db / 40.0);
            const double w = w0 (hz, sr), cw = std::cos (w), sw = std::sin (w);
            const double al = sw / 2.0 * std::sqrt (2.0), sa = 2.0 * std::sqrt (A) * al;
            set (A * ((A + 1) + (A - 1) * cw + sa), -2 * A * ((A - 1) + (A + 1) * cw), A * ((A + 1) + (A - 1) * cw - sa),
                 (A + 1) - (A - 1) * cw + sa, 2 * ((A - 1) - (A + 1) * cw), (A + 1) - (A - 1) * cw - sa);
        }
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  Modal resonator: a decaying rotation.  An impulse of height A rings as a
    //  sine of peak A, so mode amplitudes are set directly by the input.
    //==========================================================================
    struct Mode
    {
        float re = 0.0f, im = 0.0f;
        float c = 1.0f, s = 0.0f, r = 0.0f;
        bool  active = false;

        void reset() { re = im = 0.0f; }

        void set (double hz, float t60, double sr)
        {
            active = hz > 0.0 && hz < sr * 0.46;
            const double w = kTwoPi * hz / sr;
            c = (float) std::cos (w);
            s = (float) std::sin (w);
            r = sampleGainForT60 (t60, sr);
        }
        void setDecayOnly (float t60, double sr) { r = sampleGainForT60 (t60, sr); }

        float process (float x)
        {
            const float nr = r * (c * re - s * im) + x;
            const float ni = r * (s * re + c * im);
            re = nr; im = ni;
            return im;
        }
        float energy() const { return re * re + im * im; }
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  Raised-cosine hammer / mallet pulse.  Length in samples, area ~ amp.
    //==========================================================================
    struct Pulse
    {
        int   len = 0, pos = 0;
        float amp = 0.0f;

        void trigger (float lengthSamples, float amplitude)
        {
            len = std::max (2, (int) lengthSamples);
            pos = 0;
            amp = amplitude;
        }
        bool  running() const { return pos < len; }
        float next()
        {
            if (pos >= len) return 0.0f;
            const float ph = (float) pos / (float) len;
            ++pos;
            return amp * 0.5f * (1.0f - (float) std::cos (kTwoPi * ph));
        }
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  Exponential one-shot burst (noise clicks, chiff, thumps)
    //==========================================================================
    struct Burst
    {
        float level = 0.0f, mul = 0.0f;
        void  trigger (float amp, float t60, double sr) { level = amp; mul = sampleGainForT60 (t60, sr); }
        float next() { const float v = level; level *= mul; if (level < 1.0e-6f) level = 0.0f; return v; }
        bool  running() const { return level > 0.0f; }
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  Linear ramp smoother
    //==========================================================================
    struct Ramp
    {
        float v = 0.0f, target = 0.0f, step = 0.0f;
        int   left = 0;
        void  setNow (float x) { v = target = x; left = 0; step = 0.0f; }
        void  to (float x, int samples)
        {
            target = x;
            if (samples <= 0) { v = x; left = 0; return; }
            left = samples;
            step = (target - v) / (float) samples;
        }
        float next() { if (left > 0) { v += step; if (--left == 0) v = target; } return v; }
    };

    inline float softClip (float x) { return x / (1.0f + std::abs (x)); }

    /** Cheap tanh for the hot loops: exact at 0, smooth, |y| < 1. */
    inline float fastTanh (float x)
    {
        x = clampv (x, -4.5f, 4.5f);
        const float x2 = x * x;
        return x * (27.0f + x2) / (27.0f + 9.0f * x2);
    }

    //==========================================================================
    //  Sine table for additive models
    //==========================================================================
    struct SineTable
    {
        static constexpr int kSize = 4096;
        float t[kSize + 1];
        SineTable()
        {
            for (int i = 0; i <= kSize; ++i) t[i] = (float) std::sin (kTwoPi * (double) i / kSize);
        }
        float at (double ph) const        // ph 0..1
        {
            const double p = ph * kSize;
            const int    i = (int) p;
            const float  f = (float) (p - i);
            return t[i & (kSize - 1)] + f * (t[(i & (kSize - 1)) + 1] - t[i & (kSize - 1)]);
        }
        static const SineTable& get() { static const SineTable s; return s; }
    };
}

// C:\workspace\SONIFY PLUGIN natura\src\Models.h
#pragma once
//==============================================================================
//  Models.h  -  the thirteen archetypes and the bank a voice carries.
//
//  Archetypes are grouped by HOW THE SOUND IS MADE, not by GM family name, so
//  one root model can be edited into every instrument that shares its
//  mechanism (one Air Jet becomes a flute, a recorder or a pan flute).
//==============================================================================
#include "ModelsKeys.h"
#include "ModelsOrgan.h"
#include "ModelsStrings.h"
#include "ModelsWind.h"

namespace natura
{
    enum class Archetype
    {
        StruckString = 0, TineEP, StruckBar, Tonewheel, PipeOrgan, FreeReed,
        PluckedString, BowedString, LipReed, SingleReed, DoubleReed, AirJet, Synth,
        kCount
    };

    constexpr int kNumArchetypes = (int) Archetype::kCount;

    inline const char* archetypeName (int a)
    {
        static const char* names[kNumArchetypes] = {
            "STRUCK STRING", "TINE / REED EP", "STRUCK BAR", "TONEWHEEL ORGAN", "PIPE ORGAN", "FREE REED",
            "PLUCKED STRING", "BOWED STRING", "LIP REED (BRASS)", "SINGLE REED", "DOUBLE REED", "AIR JET", "SYNTH"
        };
        return names[std::min (kNumArchetypes - 1, std::max (0, a))];
    }

    //==========================================================================
    //  SYNTH: the Bambino two-oscillator engine (Grex SOUND ENGINE).
    //  The shared sections act as macros on it: strength = drive, hardness =
    //  brightness, noise = noise, decay = filter-envelope decay, damping =
    //  darker, inharmonicity = FM, odd/even = pulse width.
    //==========================================================================
    class SynthModel final : public ModelBase
    {
    public:
        void prepare (double sampleRate) override { sr = sampleRate; reset(); }
        void reset() override { v = {}; }
        bool isSustained() const override { return false; }
        Dynamics dynamics() const override { return Dynamics::Struck; }

        void start (const ModelIn& in, bool legato) override
        {
            seed = seed * 1664525u + 1013904223u + (std::uint32_t) in.note;
            oscengine::noteOn (v, in.velocity, seed, legato);
        }

        void release (const ModelIn&) override { oscengine::release (v); }

        void render (const ModelIn& in, float* out, int n) override
        {
            if (in.osc == nullptr) { std::fill (out, out + n, 0.0f); return; }
            oscengine::Params p = *in.osc;
            p.drive  = dsp::clampv (p.drive + (in.strength - 0.5f) * 0.8f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            p.cutoff = dsp::clampv (p.cutoff + (in.hardness - 0.5f) * 0.4f - (in.damping - 0.5f) * 0.4f + in.bright * 0.25f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            p.noise  = dsp::clampv (p.noise + std::max (0.0f, in.noise - 0.2f) * 0.5f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            p.envD   = dsp::clampv (p.envD + (in.decay - 0.5f) * 0.5f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            p.fm     = dsp::clampv (p.fm + std::max (0.0f, in.inharm - 0.2f) * 0.6f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            for (int o = 0; o < 2; ++o)
                p.pw[o] = dsp::clampv (p.pw[o] + (in.oddEven - 0.5f) * 0.6f, 0.05f, 0.95f);
            oscengine::prepareBlock (v, p, sr);
            for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
                out[i] = oscengine::render (v, p, (double) in.freq, in.note, sr) * 0.6f;
        }

    private:
        oscengine::Voice v;
        std::uint32_t seed = 0x1234567u;
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  The bank: one instance of every model, so switching archetype never
    //  allocates on the audio thread.  Only the active one runs.
    //==========================================================================
    class ModelBank
    {
    public:
        void prepare (double sampleRate)
        {
            for (auto* m : all()) m->prepare (sampleRate);
        }
        void reset() { for (auto* m : all()) m->reset(); }

        ModelBase& get (Archetype a)
        {
            switch (a)
            {
                case Archetype::StruckString:  return struck;
                case Archetype::TineEP:        return tine;
                case Archetype::StruckBar:     return bar;
                case Archetype::Tonewheel:     return wheel;
                case Archetype::PipeOrgan:     return pipe;
                case Archetype::FreeReed:      return freeReed;
                case Archetype::PluckedString: return plucked;
                case Archetype::BowedString:   return bowed;
                case Archetype::LipReed:       return lip;
                case Archetype::SingleReed:    return single;
                case Archetype::DoubleReed:    return dbl;
                case Archetype::AirJet:        return jet;
                case Archetype::Synth:
                default:                       return synth;
            }
        }

    private:
        std::array<ModelBase*, kNumArchetypes> all()
        {
            return { &struck, &tine, &bar, &wheel, &pipe, &freeReed, &plucked, &bowed, &lip, &single, &dbl, &jet, &synth };
        }

        StruckStringModel  struck;
        TineModel          tine;
        StruckBarModel     bar;
        TonewheelModel     wheel;
        PipeOrganModel     pipe;
        FreeReedModel      freeReed;
        PluckedStringModel plucked;
        BowedStringModel   bowed;
        LipReedModel       lip;
        SingleReedModel    single;
        DoubleReedModel    dbl;
        AirJetModel        jet;
        SynthModel         synth;
    };
}

// C:\workspace\SONIFY PLUGIN natura\src\ModelsKeys.h
#pragma once
//==============================================================================
//  ModelsKeys.h  -  the three "keyboard" archetypes.
//
//    STRUCK STRING   piano family: hammer -> 1..3 detuned waveguide strings
//                    with dispersion (stiffness), register-dependent decay,
//                    dampers, a sympathetic octave string and key-off thump.
//    TINE / REED EP  electric piano: a hammered modal tine/reed into a
//                    pickup non-linearity (Rhodes bark, Wurli bite).
//    STRUCK BAR      mallets: six modes whose ratios morph across wood,
//                    tuned metal, free bars and cantilever combs, a mallet
//                    pulse and a tube resonator.
//==============================================================================
#include "ModelBase.h"

namespace natura
{
    //==========================================================================
    //  STRUCK STRING
    //  spec: 0 hammer position, 1 strings, 2 detune, 3 sympathetic,
    //        4 key-off, 5 pedal noise (engine), 6 lid
    //==========================================================================
    class StruckStringModel final : public ModelBase
    {
    public:
        void prepare (double sampleRate) override
        {
            sr = sampleRate;
            const int maxLen = (int) (sr / 20.0) + 64;
            for (auto& l : line) l.prepare (maxLen);
            symp.prepare (maxLen);
            excBuf.prepare ((int) (sr / 20.0) + 64);
            reset();
        }

        void reset() override
        {
            for (auto& l : line) l.clear();
            symp.clear();
            excBuf.clear();
            for (int s = 0; s < 3; ++s)
            {
                lpY[s] = 0.0f;
                for (auto& a : ap[s]) a.reset();
                loopDc[s].prepare (sr, 1.0);
                loopDc[s].reset();
            }
            sympY = 0.0f;
            hammer = {};
            thump = {};
            thumpLp.reset();
            toneLp.reset();
            outDc.prepare (sr, 20.0);
            outDc.reset();
        }

        bool isSustained() const override { return false; }
        Dynamics dynamics() const override { return Dynamics::Struck; }

        void start (const ModelIn& in, bool legato) override
        {
            note = in.note;
            released = false;
            noise.seed (0xA5A5u + in.seed * 2654435761u + (std::uint32_t) in.note * 7919u);
            configure (in, ! legato);

            // hammer: harder + louder = shorter contact, brighter tone
            const float hard = dsp::clampv (in.hardness * 0.55f + in.velocity * 0.45f
                                            - in.soft * 0.25f + in.bright * 0.2f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            const float msFree = dsp::lerp (4.5f, 0.6f, hard);
            const float ms     = std::min (msFree, 0.85f * 1000.0f / std::max (20.0f, in.freq));   // treble hammers are light and quick
            const float lenS   = (float) (ms * 0.001 * sr);
            const float treble = 1.0f + dsp::clampv ((float) (in.note - 72) / 36.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            const float amp    = std::pow (in.velocity, 1.4f) * (0.45f + in.strength) * treble * (legato ? 0.5f : 1.0f);
            hammer.trigger (lenS, amp * 24.0f * (float) (sr / 48000.0) / std::max (8.0f, (float) (msFree * 0.001 * sr)));
            hammerNoise = in.noise * 0.35f;
        }

        void release (const ModelIn& in) override
        {
            released = true;
            configure (in, false);
            if (in.spec[4] > 0.001f && note < 89)
                thump.trigger (in.spec[4] * 0.08f * (0.4f + in.velocity), 0.035f, sr);
        }

        void render (const ModelIn& in, float* out, int n) override
        {
            if (std::abs (in.freq - lastFreq) > 0.01f || in.pedal != lastPedal || in.released != released
                || in.damping != lastDamp || in.decay != lastDecay)
            {
                released = in.released;
                configure (in, false);
            }

            const float posD   = std::max (2.0f, period * dsp::lerp (0.04f, 0.22f, in.spec[0]));
            const float lid    = in.spec[6];
            const float sympLv = in.spec[3];
            const float inv    = 1.0f / std::sqrt ((float) nStrings);

            for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
            {
                // excitation: hammer pulse with a little felt noise, comb-filtered by position
                float e = hammer.next();
                if (e != 0.0f) e *= 1.0f + hammerNoise * noise.next();
                excBuf.write (e);
                const float ex = e - 0.9f * excBuf.tap (posD);

                float sum = 0.0f;
                for (int s = 0; s < nStrings; ++s)
                {
                    const float v = line[s].tap (len[s]);
                    lpY[s] = (1.0f - lpA) * v + lpA * lpY[s];
                    float y = lpY[s] * g[s];
                    for (int k = 0; k < nAp; ++k) y = ap[s][k].process (y);
                    y = loopDc[s].process (y);      // a string has no DC mode
                    line[s].write (y + ex);
                    sum += v;
                }
                sum *= inv;

                // sympathetic octave string, fed lightly from the main strings
                if (sympLv > 0.001f)
                {
                    const float v = symp.tap (sympLen);
                    sympY = 0.5f * v + 0.5f * sympY;
                    symp.write (sympY * sympG + sum * 0.015f * sympLv);
                    sum += v * sympLv * 0.6f;
                }

                // key-off thump
                if (thump.running())
                    sum += thumpLp.process (thump.next() * noise.next());

                // lid: open = more top end
                sum = outDc.process (sum);
                const float low = toneLp.process (sum);
                out[i] = (low + (0.45f + lid * 0.9f) * (sum - low)) * 1.35f;
            }
        }

    private:
        void configure (const ModelIn& in, bool fresh)
        {
            lastFreq = in.freq;  lastPedal = in.pedal;  lastDamp = in.damping;  lastDecay = in.decay;
            const float f0 = dsp::clampv (in.freq, 20.0f, (float) sr * 0.3f);
            period = (float) (sr / f0);

            // how many strings: the register decides the ceiling, the knob the count
            int want = 1 + (int) std::lround (in.spec[1] * 2.0f);
            const int regMax = in.note < 34 ? 1 : (in.note < 49 ? 2 : 3);
            want = std::min (want, regMax);
            if (in.soft > 0.5f) want = std::max (1, want - 1);
            if (fresh || want != nStrings)
            {
                if (fresh) for (auto& l : line) l.clear();
                nStrings = want;
            }

            // decay: long in the bass, short in the treble
            float t60 = 16.0f * std::pow (0.965f, (float) (in.note - 21));
            t60 = dsp::clampv (t60, 0.45f, 16.0f) * std::pow (2.0f, (in.decay - 0.5f) * 3.0f) * in.decayMul;
            t60 *= 1.0f - 0.92f * in.dampAdd;

            const bool hasDamper = in.note < 89;
            if (released && hasDamper)
            {
                const float damped = in.note < 48 ? 0.22f : 0.11f;
                t60 = std::exp (dsp::lerp (std::log (damped), std::log (t60), dsp::clampv (in.pedal, 0.0f, 1.0f)));
            }

            // loop low-pass: the string's own losses
            float a = 0.04f + 0.55f * in.damping + (in.note < 40 ? 0.15f * (40 - in.note) / 40.0f : 0.0f);
            a *= dsp::clampv (std::pow (300.0f / f0, 0.6f), 0.15f, 1.0f);    // per-period loss shrinks up the keyboard
            a += 0.3f * in.dampAdd;
            lpA = dsp::clampv (a - in.bright * 0.1f, 0.0f, 0.9f);

            // stiffness: allpass dispersion, strongest at the extremes of the keyboard
            const float regF = 0.45f + 0.55f * std::min (1.0f, std::abs ((float) in.note - 62.0f) / 46.0f);
            float c = -(0.08f + 0.62f * in.inharm) * regF;
            const double w = dsp::kTwoPi * f0 / sr;
            const float lpD = dsp::OnePoleLP::phaseDelay (lpA, w);

            nAp = 4;
            float apD = dsp::Allpass1::phaseDelay (c, w);
            while (nAp > 0 && period - lpD - apD * (float) nAp < 3.0f) --nAp;
            if (nAp == 0) c = 0.0f;
            for (int s = 0; s < 3; ++s) for (auto& f : ap[s]) f.c = c;

            // in the treble the loop runs thousands of times a second: never let
            // the loss filter alone take more per pass than the decay allows
            {
                const float need = dsp::loopGainForT60 (t60, f0) / 0.9999f;
                for (int it = 0; it < 12 && lpA > 0.0005f
                     && dsp::OnePoleLP::magnitude (lpA, w) < need; ++it)
                    lpA *= 0.6f;
            }

            const float spread = in.spec[2] * 8.0f;           // cents
            const float cents[3] = { 0.0f, spread, -spread * 0.6f };
            for (int s = 0; s < 3; ++s)
            {
                const float fs = f0 * std::pow (2.0f, cents[s] / 1200.0f);
                const double ws = dsp::kTwoPi * fs / sr;
                const float  ps = (float) (sr / fs);
                const float  dLp = dsp::OnePoleLP::phaseDelay (lpA, ws);
                const float  dAp = nAp > 0 ? dsp::Allpass1::phaseDelay (c, ws) * (float) nAp : 0.0f;
                // the in-loop DC blocker (1 Hz) only leads the lowest fundamentals by a
                // few cents; compensating it would detune every upper partial instead
                len[s] = std::max (2.0f, ps - dLp - dAp);
                const float mag = dsp::OnePoleLP::magnitude (lpA, ws) * dsp::FracDelay::lagrangeMag (len[s], ws);
                g[s] = std::min (0.99995f, dsp::loopGainForT60 (t60, fs) / std::max (0.05f, mag));
            }

            // sympathetic octave string
            const float f2 = std::min (f0 * 2.0f, (float) sr * 0.3f);
            const double w2 = dsp::kTwoPi * f2 / sr;
            sympLen = std::max (2.0f, (float) (sr / f2) - dsp::OnePoleLP::phaseDelay (0.5f, w2));
            sympG   = std::min (0.9999f, dsp::loopGainForT60 (t60 * 1.6f, f2)
                                         / std::max (0.05f, dsp::OnePoleLP::magnitude (0.5f, w2) * dsp::FracDelay::lagrangeMag (sympLen, w2)));

            toneLp.setCutoff (1500.0, sr);
            thumpLp.setCutoff (260.0, sr);
        }

        dsp::FracDelay line[3], symp, excBuf;
        dsp::Allpass1  ap[3][4];
        float lpY[3] = {}, len[3] = { 100, 100, 100 }, g[3] = { 0.99f, 0.99f, 0.99f };
        float lpA = 0.2f, period = 100.0f, sympLen = 50.0f, sympG = 0.99f, sympY = 0.0f;
        int   nStrings = 1, nAp = 0, note = 60;
        float hammerNoise = 0.0f;
        float lastFreq = -1.0f, lastPedal = -1.0f, lastDamp = -1.0f, lastDecay = -1.0f;
        bool  released = false;
        dsp::Pulse hammer;
        dsp::Burst thump;
        dsp::DCBlocker loopDc[3], outDc;
        dsp::OnePoleLP thumpLp, toneLp;
        dsp::Noise noise;
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  TINE / REED ELECTRIC PIANO
    //  spec: 0 type (Rhodes..Wurli), 1 tine chime, 2 pickup, 3 bark,
    //        4 tremolo rate (engine), 5 tremolo depth (engine), 6 key-off
    //==========================================================================
    class TineModel final : public ModelBase
    {
    public:
        void prepare (double sampleRate) override { sr = sampleRate; reset(); }

        void reset() override
        {
            for (auto& m : modes) m.reset();
            hammer = {};
            keyoff = {};
            keyLp.reset();
        }

        bool isSustained() const override { return false; }
        Dynamics dynamics() const override { return Dynamics::Struck; }

        void start (const ModelIn& in, bool legato) override
        {
            note = in.note;
            released = false;
            noise.seed (0x51u + in.seed * 2654435761u + (std::uint32_t) in.note * 131u);
            configure (in);
            const float hard = dsp::clampv (in.hardness * 0.5f + in.velocity * 0.5f + in.bright * 0.2f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            const float lenS = (float) (dsp::lerp (2.8f, 0.45f, hard) * 0.001 * sr);
            hammerLen = lenS;
            const float strike = std::pow (in.velocity, 1.3f) * (0.4f + in.strength * 1.2f) * (legato ? 0.4f : 1.0f);
            hammer.trigger (lenS, strike);
            velNow = in.velocity;
        }

        void release (const ModelIn& in) override
        {
            released = true;
            configure (in);
            if (in.spec[6] > 0.001f)
                keyoff.trigger (in.spec[6] * 0.05f, 0.03f, sr);
        }

        void render (const ModelIn& in, float* out, int n) override
        {
            if (std::abs (in.freq - lastFreq) > 0.01f || in.pedal != lastPedal || in.released != released
                || in.decay != lastDecay)
            {
                released = in.released;
                configure (in);
            }

            const float type  = in.spec[0];
            const float drive = 0.7f + in.spec[3] * 2.6f * (0.35f + velNow);
            const float p     = (in.spec[2] - 0.5f) * 1.5f;
            const float tp    = std::tanh (p);
            const float norm  = 1.0f / (0.55f + drive * 0.45f);
            const float hn    = 2.0f / std::max (2.0f, hammerLen);

            for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
            {
                const float h = hammer.next() * hn;
                float sum = 0.0f;
                for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
                    if (modes[k].active) sum += modes[k].process (h * amp[k]);

                // pickup: asymmetric for the tine (even harmonics, the "bark"),
                // symmetric and harder for the reed (odd harmonics, the "bite")
                const float x  = sum * drive;
                const float rh = std::tanh (x + p) - tp;
                const float xc = dsp::clampv (x, -1.6f, 1.6f);
                const float wu = xc - 0.26f * xc * xc * xc;
                float y = dsp::lerp (rh, wu, type) * norm;

                if (keyoff.running()) y += keyLp.process (keyoff.next() * noise.next());
                out[i] = y * 0.5f;
            }
        }

    private:
        void configure (const ModelIn& in)
        {
            lastFreq = in.freq;  lastPedal = in.pedal;  lastDecay = in.decay;
            const float f0   = in.freq;
            const float type = in.spec[0];
            const float chime = in.spec[1];

            // Rhodes: tine + tonebar + cantilever overtones.  Wurli: reed overtones, shorter.
            const float ratio[4] = { 1.0f, dsp::lerp (2.0f, 3.0f, type), 6.27f, 17.55f };
            amp[0] = 1.0f;
            amp[1] = dsp::lerp (0.12f, 0.04f, type);
            amp[2] = chime * dsp::lerp (0.55f, 0.40f, type);
            amp[3] = chime * dsp::lerp (0.20f, 0.12f, type);

            float t60 = dsp::clampv (6.5f * std::pow (0.968f, (float) (in.note - 36)), 0.6f, 9.0f);
            t60 *= dsp::lerp (1.0f, 0.55f, type) * std::pow (2.0f, (in.decay - 0.5f) * 3.0f) * in.decayMul;
            t60 *= 1.0f - 0.9f * in.dampAdd;
            float tChime = dsp::lerp (0.30f, 0.18f, type) * (0.5f + in.decay);

            if (released)
            {
                const float k = dsp::clampv (in.pedal, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                t60    = std::exp (dsp::lerp (std::log (0.12f), std::log (t60), k));
                tChime = std::min (tChime, t60);
            }

            const float damp = 1.0f - 0.6f * in.damping;
            modes[0].set (f0 * ratio[0], t60, sr);
            modes[1].set (f0 * ratio[1], t60 * 0.6f, sr);
            modes[2].set (f0 * ratio[2], tChime * damp, sr);
            modes[3].set (f0 * ratio[3], tChime * 0.3f * damp, sr);
            keyLp.setCutoff (900.0, sr);
        }

        dsp::Mode  modes[4];
        float      amp[4] = { 1, 0.1f, 0.3f, 0.1f };
        dsp::Pulse hammer;
        dsp::Burst keyoff;
        dsp::OnePoleLP keyLp;
        dsp::Noise noise;
        float hammerLen = 10.0f, velNow = 0.8f;
        float lastFreq = -1.0f, lastPedal = -1.0f, lastDecay = -1.0f;
        int   note = 60;
        bool  released = false;
    };

    //==========================================================================
    //  STRUCK BAR
    //  spec: 0 mallet, 1 material, 2 strike position, 3 resonator tube,
    //        4 motor rate (engine), 5 motor depth (engine)
    //==========================================================================
    class StruckBarModel final : public ModelBase
    {
    public:
        static constexpr int kModes = 6;

        void prepare (double sampleRate) override { sr = sampleRate; reset(); }

        void reset() override
        {
            for (auto& m : modes) m.reset();
            tube.reset();
            mallet = {};
        }

        bool isSustained() const override { return false; }
        Dynamics dynamics() const override { return Dynamics::Struck; }

        void start (const ModelIn& in, bool /*legato*/) override
        {
            note = in.note;
            released = false;
            noise.seed (0xBA12u + in.seed * 2654435761u + (std::uint32_t) in.note * 977u);
            configure (in);

            const float hard = dsp::clampv (in.spec[0] * 0.6f + in.hardness * 0.4f + in.bright * 0.25f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            float ms = dsp::lerp (6.0f, 0.25f, hard) * dsp::lerp (1.15f, 0.8f, in.velocity);
            ms = std::min (ms, 0.7f * 1000.0f / std::max (20.0f, in.freq));     // small bars, short contact
            malletLen = (float) (ms * 0.001 * sr);
            mallet.trigger (malletLen, std::pow (in.velocity, 1.2f) * (0.4f + in.strength * 1.2f));
            clickNoise = in.noise * 0.3f * hard;

            // spectral weighting: a soft mallet barely reaches the upper modes
            const float tilt = dsp::lerp (2.2f, 0.6f, hard);
            for (int k = 0; k < kModes; ++k)
            {
                float a = std::pow (1.0f / ratio[k], tilt);
                if (k > 0) a *= dsp::lerp (0.35f, 1.25f, in.spec[2]);
                weight[k] = a;
            }
        }

        void release (const ModelIn& in) override
        {
            released = true;
            configure (in);
        }

        void render (const ModelIn& in, float* out, int n) override
        {
            if (std::abs (in.freq - lastFreq) > 0.01f || in.pedal != lastPedal || in.released != released
                || in.spec[1] != lastMat || in.decay != lastDecay || in.dampAdd != lastDampAdd)
            {
                released = in.released;
                configure (in);
            }

            const float hn  = 2.0f / std::max (2.0f, malletLen);
            const float tubeLv = in.spec[3];

            for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
            {
                float e = mallet.next() * hn;
                if (e != 0.0f) e *= 1.0f + clickNoise * noise.next();
                float sum = 0.0f;
                for (int k = 0; k < kModes; ++k)
                    if (modes[k].active) sum += modes[k].process (e * weight[k]);
                if (tubeLv > 0.001f)
                    sum += tube.process (sum) * tubeLv * 1.4f;     // resonator tube: a narrow lift at the fundamental
                out[i] = sum * 0.42f;
            }
        }

    private:
        void configure (const ModelIn& in)
        {
            lastFreq = in.freq;  lastPedal = in.pedal;  lastMat = in.spec[1];  lastDecay = in.decay;  lastDampAdd = in.dampAdd;

            static const float sets[5][kModes] = {
                { 1.0f, 3.99f, 9.97f,  18.0f,  27.0f,  38.0f  },   // tuned wood (marimba)
                { 1.0f, 3.0f,  6.0f,   9.8f,   14.0f,  19.0f  },   // xylophone
                { 1.0f, 4.0f,  10.0f,  18.5f,  28.0f,  40.0f  },   // tuned metal (vibes)
                { 1.0f, 2.756f,5.404f, 8.933f, 13.34f, 18.64f },   // free bar (glock, celesta)
                { 1.0f, 6.27f, 17.55f, 34.39f, 56.84f, 84.91f }    // cantilever comb (music box)
            };
            static const float baseT60[5] = { 1.3f, 0.75f, 6.0f, 3.2f, 2.2f };
            static const float decExp[5]  = { 1.25f, 1.0f, 0.85f, 0.8f, 1.0f };

            const float m = dsp::clampv (in.spec[1], 0.0f, 1.0f) * 4.0f;
            const int   i0 = std::min (3, (int) m);
            const float fr = m - (float) i0;
            for (int k = 0; k < kModes; ++k)
                ratio[k] = dsp::lerp (sets[i0][k], sets[i0 + 1][k], fr);

            float t0 = std::exp (dsp::lerp (std::log (baseT60[i0]), std::log (baseT60[i0 + 1]), fr));
            const float de = dsp::lerp (decExp[i0], decExp[i0 + 1], fr);
            t0 *= std::pow (0.972f, (float) (in.note - 60)) * std::pow (2.0f, (in.decay - 0.5f) * 3.0f) * in.decayMul;
            t0  = dsp::clampv (t0, 0.08f, 30.0f) * (1.0f - 0.95f * in.dampAdd);

            const bool hasDamper = in.spec[1] >= 0.3f && in.spec[1] < 0.9f;
            if (released && hasDamper)
                t0 = std::exp (dsp::lerp (std::log (0.18f), std::log (t0), dsp::clampv (in.pedal, 0.0f, 1.0f)));

            const float dampHi = 1.0f + in.damping * 2.0f;
            for (int k = 0; k < kModes; ++k)
            {
                const float tk = t0 / std::pow (ratio[k], de * dampHi * 0.5f + 0.25f);
                modes[k].set (in.freq * ratio[k], std::max (0.01f, tk), sr);
            }
            tube.bandpass (in.freq, 24.0, sr);
        }

        dsp::Mode  modes[kModes];
        dsp::Biquad tube;
        float      ratio[kModes] = { 1, 4, 10, 18, 27, 38 };
        float      weight[kModes] = { 1, 0.3f, 0.1f, 0.05f, 0.02f, 0.01f };
        dsp::Pulse mallet;
        dsp::Noise noise;
        float malletLen = 20.0f, clickNoise = 0.0f;
        float lastFreq = -1.0f, lastPedal = -1.0f, lastMat = -1.0f, lastDecay = -1.0f, lastDampAdd = -1.0f;
        int   note = 60;
        bool  released = false;
    };
}
